title: Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services

reading.body:
This incident is an impersonation fraud in which AI-generated video and fabricated social media profiles were used to make a real, named attorney appear to be offering immigration services he never provided. The failure did not originate inside a legitimate AI product deployment. It is an offensive use of generative tools by external actors who created synthetic content at scale, distributing it across multiple platforms before any detection occurred. The volume involved, nearly 6,500 accounts removed across TikTok, Facebook, and Instagram, shows the content spread widely before the attorney himself noticed it through incoming calls to his real office.

What made the scheme effective was the combination of a credible real identity, synthetic video that mimicked it, and a payment flow designed to leave no recourse, directing victims to cash-transfer apps and WhatsApp contacts outside the platforms' normal reporting structures. The platforms' own content moderation did not catch the accounts proactively. Detection required the attorney to hire a specialist anti-piracy firm, meaning the burden of enforcement fell on the person whose identity was stolen rather than on the platforms hosting the content.

What is not established is who operated the scheme, where it originated, or whether any platform violated its own policies in a legally actionable way. No charges, findings, or law-enforcement conclusions are reported.

reports.title: Scammers steal identity of renowned Miami attorney to target immigrants on social media
South Florida immigration attorney says AI scammers are using his identity to target immigrants
Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services
Legal resident loses thousands seeking citizenship to AI immigration attorney

summary:
Angel Leal, a South Florida immigration attorney with over 30 years of experience, has become the target of an extensive AI-powered scam operation. Criminals have created hundreds of fake videos and social media profiles using artificial intelligence to impersonate him, deceiving vulnerable immigrants into paying thousands of dollars for immigration services he never offered. The fraudulent scheme escalated dramatically over the past three months, with scammers offering services like US residency assistance for $2,200 cash payments through fake videos and testimonials.

After discovering the fraud when potential clients began calling his office, Leal hired an online anti-piracy company that successfully removed nearly 6,500 fake accounts across social media platforms, including 3,500 on TikTok, 2,400 on Facebook, and 544 on Instagram. The scams typically direct victims to contact numbers via WhatsApp and send phony contracts. Leal warned consumers to be cautious of requests for payment through apps like Venmo, Zelle, or Cash App, and emphasized his office never requests payments over the phone. He plans to contact local and federal authorities to investigate the scam's origins.
